required_observations: Every material factual claim and its registered evidence reference.
program_checks: Require evidence_id in registry; resolve raw_reference.record_id/json_pointer; verify content_sha256 against the actual alert or returned record.
Tool and knowledge references require a completed call_id in this run and the frozen snapshot; values must agree with the referenced payload, not just exist.
Interpretations and model-generated text are not source facts.
model_explanation: No model explanation can repair an invalid source or contradict the referenced value.
conflict_handling: Forged references or conflicting source values block a definitive conclusion.
unverifiable: Missing/truncated source or unresolved pointer is unknown; a known hash/value mismatch is unmet, never met.

required_observations: Event identities, host, process instance identifiers, event timestamps and investigated activity window.
program_checks: Associate all material behavior to the same host and process instance using a stable GUID or an equally explicit instance linkage; PID or IP alone is insufficient.
Check occurred_at lies in the relevant activity window and observed/published timestamps do not exceed as_of.
model_explanation: Explain the explicit correlation chain and the limits of any indirect association.
conflict_handling: Inconsistent instance identity or a known out-of-window event is unmet; unresolved association conflicts block TP and FP.
unverifiable: Absent instance linkage or timestamps is unknown; do not substitute a shared IP, account or PID.

required_observations: Source-recorded attack behavior chain or a high-quality direct observation of unauthorized malicious behavior.
program_checks: Require grounded actual behavior/content and linked effects, not a label alone; identify which attack-relevant predicate was observed.
TI reputation/unknown, ATT&CK mappings, detector_claim, PowerShell execution, encoded metadata and absent approval cannot independently satisfy this gate.
TI verdict fields are not scored as host behavior; actual script or independently correlated effects must supply the attack basis.
model_explanation: Explain why the observed behavior demonstrates malicious execution and what benign mechanism it excludes.
conflict_handling: High-quality contrary behavior or an unresolved authorized explanation blocks met; source coverage loss is not attack evidence.
unverifiable: Missing script/body/effects or only weak indicators yields unknown; verified benign behavior inconsistent with the proposed attack basis yields unmet.

required_observations: Strongest plausible benign explanation, corresponding approval/job records and current execution details.
program_checks: Check a concrete competing explanation against host/account/time/job/script or hash/parameters and actual effects.
A negative approval lookup is valid only with complete approval-register coverage for the same host and activity window; an equivalent complete history approval check is accepted.
No approval alone cannot establish malicious behavior; missing archive, partial coverage and unavailable history cannot prove no approval.
model_explanation: Explain how the strongest benign hypothesis was tested and why it fails to explain the material attack behavior.
conflict_handling: Unresolved high-quality approval or behavior conflict blocks met; do not discard a conflicting record because it opposes the leading hypothesis.
unverifiable: No tested benign explanation or incomplete approval coverage is unknown.

required_observations: Source quality, independence_group, canonical fact_key, coverage scope and missing sources.
program_checks: Deduplicate mirrored facts by fact_key; the same fact obtained through asset and history is not two independent supports.
Verify sufficient relevant coverage and quality for each material claim; incomplete coverage cannot establish absence.
Do not require a fixed number of tools or sources: one complete verifiable high-quality behavior record can suffice; many repeated weak records cannot.
model_explanation: Describe independent corroboration, dependencies and exactly which event scope was checked.
conflict_handling: Unresolved source-quality/coverage conflict blocks met; adding evidence may reduce sufficiency.
unverifiable: Unknown source quality, provenance dependency or material coverage is unknown.

required_observations: Actual execution details and a positive approved operation record.
program_checks: Match actual host, account, activity time, job/task, script content or hash, and execution parameters to the approved operation.
Verify the approval time interval contains execution; a maintenance window or administrator identity alone never proves matching authorization.
model_explanation: Explain the specific approved operation and its match to this activity, not the general legitimacy of the user.
conflict_handling: A known job/hash/parameter mismatch is unmet even within a maintenance window; unresolved competing approval data blocks met.
unverifiable: Missing matching fields, missing approval archives or unavailable approval source is unknown.

required_observations: Recorded execution behavior and effects, plus the approved scope and targets.
program_checks: Verify the actual script/task behavior and same-instance network/file effects agree with the approved operation.
TI unknown/benign, lack of malicious TI, ATT&CK knowledge and periodic history cannot replace current behavior consistency.
No network records only establishes no network behavior when complete relevant scope/window coverage proves absence.
model_explanation: Explain why observed effects are within the approved operation and identify checked external/internal targets.
conflict_handling: Observed out-of-scope behavior is unmet; a high-quality unresolved contradiction blocks met.
unverifiable: Missing current behavior/effects or partial/unavailable relevant logs is unknown.

required_observations: Coverage of relevant behavior window and scope, risk counterevidence and the proposed closure claims.
program_checks: Require adequate coverage to check material exceptions and no unresolved high-quality malicious counterevidence.
Limit closure to this alert activity and checked scope; reject host-wide safety/clean claims unsupported by the investigated scope.
Unknown sources and partial empty results cannot be converted into absence; no fixed tool count grants coverage.
model_explanation: State the checked scope and unresolved facts outside it; FP recommends closure of this activity only.
conflict_handling: Unresolved high-quality counterevidence or both TP and FP groups met blocks closure; do not pick a larger confidence score.
unverifiable: Unverified relevant scope or unavailable material counterevidence source is unknown.

decision_rules: met requires all program checks verified and no unresolved material conflict; unmet means a verified contradiction; unknown means unavailable information, not a negative observation.
TP requires all TP gates met, FP group not all met and material conflicts resolved; FP requires all FP gates met, TP group not all met and material conflicts resolved.
Both groups met is conflicting_evidence: investigate the contradiction or Abstain; never select the higher score.

After a final admitted tool result, a remaining reserved finalization evaluation may produce TP/FP only if all gates are independently verified before the deadline; otherwise a hard-stop result is Abstain.

Suspicious requires neither group met, G0/G1 verified for at least one declared substantive risk pattern, unresolved decision evidence, and all affordable legal useful remaining actions assessed exhausted/unavailable; hard-stop must not be triggered.
Hard budget stop without a valid sufficient conclusion forces Abstain, preserving grounded risk flags; Suspicious cannot bypass this rule.
Only vague alert trigger facts, unresolved decisive source conflict, protocol/model failure or no verified substantive risk pattern yields Abstain; retain missing evidence and reason.
Determining gates and patterns requires implementation of mechanical checks plus scoped semantic explanation; loading this rubric is not that implementation.

required_observations: Positive approved operation and grounded current execution belonging to the same host/account/activity.
program_checks: Compare task/job, script hash/content and parameters field by field; require at least one known mismatch, stable event association and explicit references to both values.
excluded_observations: Only a maintenance window, missing approval archive, detector label or TI unknown is not a mismatch.

required_observations: Grounded same-instance external connection and reliable comparable history establishing a new target; no matching approved target explanation after an available approval check.
program_checks: Verify observed destination, external classification, newness from explicit reliable source facts/history and G0/G1 event linkage; an unavailable history does not establish newness.
excluded_observations: External IP alone, lack of TI reputation, missing network payload, unknown history and ATT&CK mapping alone do not satisfy the pattern.

scope: Family-level operational standard for alert-scoped PowerShell investigation; not a formal proof of real-world safety.
No case identifier, host, job or hidden world truth determines a gate.
Only alert, returned tool record or trusted knowledge facts may be cited; knowledge mapping is not observed attack behavior.
M2 freezes descriptions and program obligations; M7 runtime checks and M5 independent scoring remain separate implementations using this version.
